title: LightGBM inflammatory-nutritional model stratifies pneumonia risk after brain injury
summary: A LightGBM model, the best of six, used admission inflammatory-nutritional indices (PIV, PNI) and laboratory data to predict hospital-acquired pneumonia in 567 adults with traumatic brain injury at two hospitals, reaching AUC 0.815 in an independent testing cohort (n = 171). PIV was the top SHAP predictor and risk strata were associated with discharge mRS 0-2. The study is retrospective with a modest sample and prospective validation is pending.
ai_technology: LightGBM (best of six machine-learning models) on admission inflammatory-nutritional indices and laboratory data

evidence.tested: Independent testing cohort (n = 171) from a second center.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance and clinical benefit; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A gradient boosting model predicted pneumonia after brain injury from admission laboratory indices.
